A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Lean 4 statistical-learning formalization project. All 19 pages of v1 and 29 pages of v2, including their appendices, are readable and support comparison despite the changed title and layout.

before.justification: v1 reports formal proofs, theoretical regression guarantees, and development totals. It does not report experimental, simulation, user-study, or data-analysis outcomes; its regression applications are mathematical demonstrations.

after.justification: Section 5 reports original observations and retrospective analysis of the formalization workflow, including prompting failure rates and percentages of declarations requiring different levels of human intervention.

M1.justification: The mathematical formalization pipeline and Claude Code/Opus-4.5 setup are retained. Section 5 and Appendices E–F document specifications, refinement, and cleanup within the existing development workflow; they do not establish a revision to the underlying method between versions.

E1.justification: The Gaussian-analysis, Dudley, linear-regression, and l1-regression formalization tasks remain the same. The new workflow analysis concerns the existing project and Gaussian-LSI extension, without establishing additional datasets, application domains, or theorem-task coverage.

E2.justification: Section 5.1 newly compares structured TASK.md specifications with unstructured instructions lacking infrastructure pointers, reporting outcomes for both. v1 contains no corresponding empirical comparison; no competing theorem-proving systems are added.

E3.justification: v2 introduces first-attempt failure assessment and retrospective classification of declarations into four human-intervention tiers. Approximately 60 preserved specifications provide source context, but exact comparison denominators, task matching, and controls are unspecified. These are newly reported evaluation procedures, not demonstrated reruns of earlier experiments.

E4.justification: Section 5.2 and Appendix F add a detailed four-specification Gaussian-LSI case study diagnosing failed attempts and their resolution. Section 5.3 adds analysis of three incorrectly formulated targets. This substantially extends v1's discussion of mathematical implementation challenges into qualitative analysis of agent failures.

E5.justification: Neither version reports seeds, repeated-run uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals, or significance tests. v2's approximate percentages and successive specification revisions do not constitute statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v2 adds roughly 70% failure for unstructured instructions and 15% first-attempt failure with structured specifications. Table 1 reports approximately 15%, 30%, 40%, and 15% across Autonomous, Sketch-Guided, Specified, and Human-critical tiers. New qualitative outcomes include successful fourth-specification completion and degradation beyond roughly 300 authored lines per turn. These are newly reported workflow results, not demonstrated performance gains between PDFs.

T1.justification: Appendix F adds substantial mathematical derivations for the existing Gaussian-LSI density extension, including gradient convergence, convergence of squared functions, and entropy lower semicontinuity using shifted Fatou arguments. Separately, Theorem 4.1 changes from any positive radius satisfying the critical inequality to its smallest positive solution, while Appendix C.1 retains the original general Lean signature.

C1.justification: The principal Gaussian-analysis, Dudley, and regression contributions remain unchanged. Introduction contribution 4 narrows the acceleration claim: v1 contrasts approximately 500 hours with projects previously requiring years, whereas v2 removes that comparison and describes the project as one realization of effective human–AI collaboration.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive interpretations of collaboration failures: specification ambiguity rather than tactical execution is often the bottleneck, unchanged retries are ineffective, and human review must check mathematical statements themselves. Appendix E explains context-size and rewriting failure mechanisms; these operational limitations and interpretations were absent from v1.

D1.justification: Appendices E–F disclose reusable prompts, a roughly 300-line lemma target, dependency names and file locations, build-success criteria, and alternating warning/unused-have cleanup procedures. Four concrete task specifications make the previously summarized workflow substantially more reproducible. The repository access information remains equivalent.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive positioning relative to earlier Lean formalizations and statistical-learning textbooks are retained. Expanded bibliographic details for existing books do not introduce new related work or change the novelty comparison.

P1.justification: The previously brief collaboration account receives a substantial explanatory expansion through a four-part Section 5, a practical-recipe appendix, and worked specification transcripts. The title becomes AI4SLT and an impact statement is added. Most existing mathematical prose and the organization of Appendices A–D remain intact.

P2.justification: The main text changes from predominantly single-column presentation to two columns, with running headers and extensively rewrapped code listings. v2 adds the intervention table and shaded specification blocks while retaining Figures 1–2. The earlier theorem-reference table becomes Table 2 and omits the one_step_discretization row; this does not establish deletion from the library.

improvement.justification: v2 improves transparency through concrete workflow instructions, failure analyses, and the explicit Gaussian-LSI limiting argument. The gains are moderated by missing denominators and controls for the new percentages, and Section 5.3's ambiguous description of both successful misformalized proofs and persistent sorry failures. The revision makes the project easier to understand and reproduce, but provides limited evidence for broad workflow-effectiveness claims.
